title: Adaptive sellframe: cost vs latency differentiator (rough)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for a 1) seller-facing narrative and 2) two-page technical battlecard that helps platform/infra-oriented buyers understand Redwood's pragmatic routing and fallback story when capacity or SLO conflicts arise. Focus: tradeoffs (latency vs $/token), fallback policies, simple Qs for qualification, and a quick escalation checklist for trials.

Audience: sales engineers (primary), AE/field sellers (secondary), platform architects (end reader). Keep it short — usable in an email or 5-min demo.

Topline message (one-liner):
- "Redwood keeps your product online and predictable: we optimize for latency while automatically routing and degrading to lower-cost compatible model variants with transparent economics and safe fallbacks."

Slide / one-pager outline (riff):
1) Lead-in: customer problem frame (3 bullets)
   - "Spike in traffic + heavy long-context use"
   - "Budget pressure + unpredictable unit costs"
   - "Compliance/regulatory constraints across regions"
2) Our answer: adaptive routing & cost-aware fallbacks (headline + 2 visuals)
   - Visual A: routing ladder (primary model -> quantized variant -> cached response -> fallback model)
   - Visual B: per-token cost vs p95 latency chart (simple curve)
3) How it works (quick tech bullets)
   - routing policies by tag: latency-first | cost-first | region-first
   - automatic prefix/KV cache hit reuse reduces tokens by ~20-60% depending on workload (examples later)
   - quantized model variants available in the catalog; transparent perf profile attached to each version
4) Qualification checklist (for seller) — quick Qs to ask customer
   - What is your p95 latency SLO for interactive flows? (50ms / 200ms / 500ms?)
   - Typical context length (tokens)? Peak requests per second?
   - Is cost sensitivity per-request or monthly budget-oriented?
   - Any data residency or private deployment constraints?
5) Fallback policies (concrete examples)
   - Canary-friendly: 5% traffic -> primary; 95% routed to cost-tiered variant for load testing
   - Emergency fallback: if primary p95 breaches target 3x in 1m, auto-failover to next compatible variant + alert
   - Graceful degradation: shorten max tokens + increase top_p to reduce generation compute
6) Seller script snippets (quick)
   - "If latency spikes, we can transparently route to a quantized variant with 10-15% lower per-token cost and p95 within X ms; you keep the same API surface."
   - "We expose per-route token economics in Console so you can see exactly what fallback saved or costed you."
7) Quick metrics to show in trial / demo dashboard
   - tokens per request (avg/95), cache hit rate, model variant ratio, per-route $/1000 tokens, p50/p95/p99 latency.
8) Escalation checklist for pilots (two-step)
   - If customer sees >10% error or >2x p95: enable verbose traces (Console), route 30% to reserved Dedicated nodes, open SRE bridge
   - If cost beats expectation: apply batching + tighten quantization profile, re-run small eval on prompt set

Examples / short use cases (bulleted):
- Conversational agent (support chat)
  - Typical tokens: 150–600
  - Goal: sub-300ms p95, cost-sensitivity medium
  - Play: latency-first routing; keep small prefix cache; fallback to quantized variant when sustained >2x p95
- Document summarization (async)
  - Typical tokens: 2k–8k
  - Goal: cost minimization; latency relaxed (seconds ok)
  - Play: cost-first routing; prefer reservoir compute on Dedicated or offline batch; use cached embeddings + rerank

Technical cheat-sheet (for SEs) — copyable bullets to paste into email or Slack:
- "We support policy chain ordering: region->latency->cost. Policy example: region(us-east)->latency(200ms)->cost(limit 0.5$/1k tokens)->fallback(quant8)->fallback(model-small)."
- "Cache: prefix and KV cache; typical effect 20–60% tokens saved on multi-turn chat when prompts reuse system messages or user context. Measure: cache-hit-rate in Console."
- "Quantization: nv-q8* and int8 variants available; each variant has a perf profile (tokens/sec, p95) in the model catalog. We recommend small A/B with 5–10% traffic initially."

Unresolved / notes to self (things to add before next review):
- Add small benchmark table comparing 3 open-source model families across q8/int8/resnet-style runtime for 512 vs 2048 context (numbers and units).
- One-liner for procurement: how Reserved capacity discount stacks with usage for blended $/token.
- Create short animated gif showing routing ladder in Console.
- Validate exact console metric names for tokens-per-request and per-route cost (ask Observability team).

Risk and objection prep (quick responses):
- Customer: "Quantized models degrade quality" -> Answer: show eval on their prompt set (we do small rollouts with quality regression monitors + canary fallback to original model).
- Customer: "I need absolute determinism" -> Answer: deterministic inference limited; suggest Private deployment + pinned model version + stable runtime knob.
- Customer: "We can't accept silent fallback" -> Answer: explain canary & explicit fallback policy that surfaces notifications and audit logs; optional manual approval for critical routes.

Appendix: quick scripts and links (placeholders)
- Quick demo checklist: 1) Enable verbose tracing; 2) Start 100 RPS hit test with primary; 3) Turn on fallback policy; 4) Measure delta; 5) Capture per-route cost report.
- Placeholder links to Confluence playbook and perf spreadsheets (to be inserted)

Tone/format notes for final deck:
- Keep seller narrative light on deep infra detail; provide two slides for SE deep-dive with the technical cheat-sheet and an annotated Console screenshot.
- Provide copy-paste snippets for Slack/email and a one-paragraph executive summary for procurement.

Bottom-line (to end slide):
- "Redwood lets teams keep customers in-product under load by making smart, observable compromises between latency and cost — without sacrificing control."

Contact for this draft: Priya.Raman@redwood.ai (SE feedback welcome).

End of note.
